cases.purpose: passwd list and list -l over a private database with empty fields, malformed rows (6 and 8 fields, empty name, blank line), uid/gid boundaries and duplicates.
cases.oracle: passwd(5) seven colon-separated fields projected by an in-script /usr/bin/awk -F: reference (and an independent Python projection used to precompute the fixed expectations); uid_t/gid_t are unsigned 32-bit with (uid_t)-1 reserved; password status letters follow shadow-utils passwd -S (L: hash starts with ! or *, NP: empty, P: otherwise). Only private relative PHCLIB_* files are read; /etc/passwd's real 'parity' account must not be found.
cases.comparison: Exact list and list -l bytes, plus cmp against the in-script awk projection; usage error for an unknown list argument.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t passwd) == builtin ]] || { printf 'candidate passwd builtin missing\n'; exit 99; }
export PHCLIB_PASSWD=passwd.fixture PHCLIB_SHADOW=shadow.fixture PHCLIB_GROUP=group.fixture BASHPASSWD_KERNEL_SECRETS=0
/usr/bin/awk -F: 'NF == 7 && $1 != "" { print $1 }' passwd.fixture > awk.list
/usr/bin/awk -F: 'NF == 7 && $1 != "" { print $1 ":" $3 ":" $4 ":" $6 ":" $7 }' passwd.fixture > awk.long
passwd list > c.list; printf 'list-rc=%d\n' "$?"
/usr/bin/cmp -s c.list awk.list && printf 'list=awk-match\n' || printf 'list=awk-differ\n'
/usr/bin/cat c.list
passwd list -l > c.long; printf 'long-rc=%d\n' "$?"
/usr/bin/cmp -s c.long awk.long && printf 'long=awk-match\n' || printf 'long=awk-differ\n'
/usr/bin/cat c.long
passwd list -x > /dev/null 2> err; printf 'bad-arg-rc=%d\n' "$?"
/usr/bin/rm -f c.list c.long awk.list awk.long err

cases.purpose: passwd info for valid, boundary, malformed, duplicate, missing and host-only accounts, plus info usage errors.
cases.oracle: passwd(5) seven colon-separated fields projected by an in-script /usr/bin/awk -F: reference (and an independent Python projection used to precompute the fixed expectations); uid_t/gid_t are unsigned 32-bit with (uid_t)-1 reserved; password status letters follow shadow-utils passwd -S (L: hash starts with ! or *, NP: empty, P: otherwise). Only private relative PHCLIB_* files are read; /etc/passwd's real 'parity' account must not be found. The first well-formed row for a name wins; rows whose uid or gid is not a decimal below 4294967295 are not accounts.
cases.comparison: Exact status and stdout per name; stderr is not asserted here (see the success-silence case).
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t passwd) == builtin ]] || { printf 'candidate passwd builtin missing\n'; exit 99; }

cases.purpose: A successful info query for usable (P), empty (NP) and locked (L) accounts writes no diagnostic.
cases.oracle: Builtin convention: diagnostics accompany failure statuses; status letters per shadow-utils passwd -S semantics, where every state is a successful query.
cases.comparison: Exact status and stderr presence per account.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t passwd) == builtin ]] || { printf 'candidate passwd builtin missing\n'; exit 99; }
export PHCLIB_PASSWD=passwd.fixture PHCLIB_SHADOW=shadow.fixture PHCLIB_GROUP=group.fixture BASHPASSWD_KERNEL_SECRETS=0
for n in alice bob root; do
  passwd info "$n" > /dev/null 2> err; rc=$?
  [[ -s err ]] && d=yes || d=no
  printf '%s rc=%d diag=%s\n' "$n" "$rc" "$d"
done
/usr/bin/rm -f err
cases.stdout:
alice rc=0 diag=no
bob rc=0 diag=no
root rc=0 diag=no

cases.purpose: Option parsing (-, -l, --login, --no-login, --keep-env, --unsafe-keep-env, -c CMD, -cCMD, --), default target root, extra arguments, missing -c argument, unknown flags, invalid and boundary-length names, malformed account rows and an unreadable database. Every form ends before authentication: the private database has no root and no reachable target, so no terminal is opened, nothing forks and -c commands never run.
cases.oracle: su usage synopsis (su [--login|--no-login] [--keep-env] [-c CMD] [USER], default USER root as in util-linux su), the shared bash-os account-name rule (lowercase or '_' first, then [a-z0-9_-], at most 32 bytes; as documented for useradd NAME_REGEX), passwd(5) seven-field rows with decimal ids, and status 2 for usage errors versus 1 for lookup failures. Only private relative PHCLIB_* files are read.
cases.comparison: Exact status, empty stdout and diagnostic class per form (wording matched only by the documented message keys); a marker file proves -c commands never ran.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t su) == builtin ]] || { printf 'candidate su builtin missing\n'; exit 99; }
export PHCLIB_PASSWD=passwd.fixture PHCLIB_SHADOW=shadow.fixture PHCLIB_GROUP=group.fixture BASHPASSWD_KERNEL_SECRETS=0
try() {
  local label=$1; shift
  su "$@" > out 2> err; local rc=$?
  local e; e=$(< err) c=other
  case $e in
    *"no such user: "*) c="no-such-user(${e##*no such user: })" ;;
    *"invalid user: "*) c="invalid-user" ;;
    *"extra arg "*) c="extra-arg" ;;
    *"-c needs CMD"*) c="missing-cmd" ;;
    *"unknown flag: "*) c="unknown-flag" ;;
    *"cannot read passwd database"*) c="unreadable-db" ;;
    "") c=none ;;
  esac
  [[ -s out ]] && o=nonempty || o=empty
  printf '%s rc=%d stdout=%s diag=%s\n' "$label" "$rc" "$o" "$c"
}
try default 
try dash -
try l -l
try login --login
try no-login --no-login
try keep-env --keep-env
try unsafe-keep-env --unsafe-keep-env
try c-separate -c ': > ran'
try c-attached '-c: > ran'
try separator -- nosuch
try c-then-user -c ': > ran' nosuch
try login-then-user --login nosuch
try missing-c -c
try extra nosuch extra
try separator-extra -- nosuch extra
try unknown --zq
try bad-space 'Bad Name'
try empty ''
try digit-first 1abc
try dash-target -- -l
try name-32 aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
try name-33 aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
try malformed-id badid
[[ -e ran ]] && printf 'command=ran\n' || printf 'command=not-run\n'
PHCLIB_PASSWD=absent.fixture try unreadable alice
su --help > help.out 2> err; printf 'help rc=%d first=[%s] diag=%s\n' "$?" "$(/usr/bin/head -n 1 help.out)" "$([[ -s err ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
/usr/bin/rm -f out err help.out
